steps: Clearances & floor protection
Hold the lettered wall and corner clearances from the p. 8 table and drawing. On a combustible floor, lay a UL 1618 Type 1 non-combustible shield (min. 35" × 42.125" USA, 45.25" × 52.125" Canada).

Before starting, consult the authority having jurisdiction about a permit (cover page). Minimum clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. In the USA the shield extends 16" in front of and 8" to either side of the loading door, and 2" beyond each side of the chimney connector.
Combustion air
In tight homes, balance intake air against HRVs, air handlers, range hoods and dryers. A fresh air inlet into the stove room is recommended to prevent smoke spillage and CO.

Optional Outside Air Kits: 3" S.Z1726B or 4" S.Z1726. The hose can run through an outside wall or up through the floor, must stay open, and must never penetrate a wall above the bottom of the rear intake channel. Consult an HVAC specialist.
Chimney & connector

6" listed UL-103HT / CAN/ULC-S629 chimney or code-approved masonry with liner; 6" 24 MSG steel connector with sheet metal screws at every joint, support package through ceilings, listed thimble through combustible walls.

Never share a flue with another appliance. Buy every prefab component (support or wall pass through, tee, fire stops, insulation shield, flashing, cap) from the same chimney manufacturer. An interior chimney is recommended; build a chase around an exterior one. Keep a vapor barrier where the chimney penetrates the exterior. In Canada, follow CSA B365-M87.
Masonry chimney prep
Have it inspected by a certified professional and cleaned: no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage. A stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, is recommended.
A connector through a combustible wall needs approved methods: NFPA minimum standards in the USA, CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada.
Chimney height
15 ft minimum stove top to termination up to 1000 ft elevation, more with elbows or altitude (p. 12 table). At least 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.
Placement & power

Never in a bedroom; in Canada, not in an alcove or fireplace. The optional fan kit plugs into a grounded three-hole receptacle; don't cut the ground prong or route the cord in front of or under the stove.

Freestanding space heater only, in an insulated, habitable room; not designed for an uninsulated concrete basement or a shop/garage.

Note: on fireplace installs, the certification label says "Not to be installed in any fireplace" (p. 4); p. 13 bars alcove and fireplace installs in Canada and, for the USA, says only to adhere to minimum safe clearances.
Mobile home install
Outside Air Kit plus Fan Kit or Rear Shield Kit, roof exit only, double wall close clearance pipe. Fasten the stove to the floor with the kit's tie-downs.
Side shields & door
Side shields lift off after the cover plate and screws (remove the bypass handle before the right shield). The loading door comes off its two hinge shoulder bolts.

1. Side shield: unfasten the two top screws (A) and lift off the cover plate, unfasten the remaining x4 screws, then grasp the shield at the upper and lower cut-outs and lift it up.
  2. Door (p. 15): 1/4" allen key in the shoulder bolt head on top of the upper hinge, 9/16" wrench on the nut below; turn the bolt counter-clockwise to remove the nut; repeat on the lower hinge; hold the door and pull out the bolts.
  3. Reinstall in reverse order. Never operate the stove with the door off or open.
First fire
Confirm every firebrick is in place and build the fire on the brick, no grate. Burn low for several hours to cure the paint, with a door or window open for the odor and smoke.
Hand-over
Complete the installer details on the last page (dealer, installer, date installed, serial number) and leave the manual with the homeowner.

panels.title: Not enough heat
items: Green or wet wood → check it with a moisture meter
Not enough fuel → load fully; a full load burns no hotter than the thermostat setting
Combustor plugged, coated or not working → clean, test or replace it
Poor draft or gusting downdraft → measure with a manometer; wind-resistant cap
Tightly sealed house → open a window slightly or add an outside air kit

panels.title: Too much heat
items: Bypass door left open → close it
Thermostat set too high → lower it
Door gasket leaking → replace gasket and/or adjust door
Excessive chimney draft → measure with a manometer; install a cap
Wood too small → use larger pieces

panels.title: Smoke spills when loading
items: Spark arrestor screen plugged → clean to bare metal wire
Chimney too cold → use double wall stove pipe
Not enough vertical rise → 36" minimum before elbows; two 45s instead of a 90
Chimney not drafting → thermostat high, bypass open, door closed, wait 5-10 minutes

panels.title: Thermometer won't reach Active
items: Improper operation → check thermostat setting and procedure
Obstruction in chimney or cap → clean the chimney
Combustor plugged or not working → clean, test or replace
Bypass door leaking or not closing → clean around it; adjust or replace gasket

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build the fire right on the bottom firebrick, never on a grate.

  1. Check that all the firebricks are in place.
  2. Turn the thermostat to HIGH and the fan (if you have one) off.
  3. Open the bypass, then open the loading door.
  4. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front, then crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, leaving air gaps.
  5. Light it and leave the door cracked open. Don't leave the stove unattended.
  6. Once the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  7. Latch the door. When the combustor temperature starts to climb, close the bypass and turn the fans on high (if equipped).
  8. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer is in the active zone, open the bypass and door and fill the stove, wood as far back as possible. Latch the door, close the bypass.
  9. Leave it on HIGH until the fire is well established and the needle is in the ACTIVE zone (at least 500F).
  10. Then turn the thermostat down gradually to the heat you want. If the needle falls to INACTIVE, turn it back up.
  11. Turn the fan on after the initial warm-up.
First fires: the paint cures with a strong smell and some smoke. Burn low for several hours and open a door or window. A change in paint color is normal.
Leaving the door open after the wood has caught can cause early failure of the catalytic combustor.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
If the thermometer needle is still in the ACTIVE zone, reload like this. If it has dropped to INACTIVE, start again with the lighting steps.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to HIGH and wait a few minutes for the airflow to settle.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes. This helps keep smoke out of the room.
  3. Crack the loading door open to let room air in. Give it a minute.
  4. Slowly open the door and load. If smoke spills out, close the door a little until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on HIGH until the fire is well established, then turn it down.

On low settings you may see very little flame. That's fine: a needle that stays in the active zone means the burn is still going.

The thermometer is only one clue for when to reload. An empty firebox or a cooling room count too. Only load wood inside the shaded area the manual shows on p. 19.

Dark glass? Long, very low burns leave creosote on the glass. Run the stove on HIGH for about 30 minutes to burn most of it off.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass and fan
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

It's at the upper right rear corner. At HIGH the stove burns fastest and gives the most heat. Turn it counter-clockwise for less. Make changes gradually; fast changes can make the thermostat work poorly. The minimum low-burn setting is set at the factory and must not be altered.

Turned down too low, the fire can go out or the combustor can stop working. Turn it back up and let the fire recover. The tested low-burn knob position is shown as a diagram on p. 22.

Bypass handle

On the right side. Pointing forward means the bypass is open: smoke skips the catalytic combustor, for lighting and reloading. To close it, turn the handle clockwise until it points to the rear, then push down until it clicks.

Fan (optional)

Keep the fans off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature. About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match the fan speed to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

Note: p. 16 says to keep the fan off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature; the lighting steps on p. 20 say to switch it on high once the door is latched and the combustor warms (step 7), and to turn it on after the initial warm-up (step 11).

thermometer.title: Reading the catalytic thermometer
thermometer.html:
The dial on top of the stove reads the exhaust after it passes through the catalytic combustor. Keep the needle in the ACTIVE zone.

  • ACTIVE: the combustor is above 500F and burning clean. It often runs past 1000F.
  • INACTIVE: below 500F, so the burn isn't clean. Turn the thermostat up and let the fire re-establish.

If you have a fan, switch it off before you read the dial.

Note: p. 18 says to turn the fan off about 5 minutes before you read the dial; p. 29 and p. 35 say 10 minutes.

Is the combustor working?

Look at it at least three times each heating season. Quick check: open the bypass, wait a few minutes and watch the chimney, then close it. You should see clearly less smoke with the bypass closed. If the needle won't reach ACTIVE at a medium-low setting over 3 burn cycles, the combustor may need cleaning or replacing, or the thermometer itself may be off. Ask your Blaze King dealer.

Turning the thermostat down can make the combustor temperature climb for up to several hours. That's normal.

On mild spring or fall days, keep the setting high enough to hold the needle in the active zone: turn it up, wait 15 minutes, check again.

wood.title: Burning the right wood
wood.html:
Burn natural cord wood only, at 20% moisture or lower: split, stacked so air reaches it, and kept out of rain and snow for at least 24 months. Wet wood wastes heat and builds creosote fast. Hardwood and softwood both burn well; dense hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each one down the middle.
  2. On the split face, measure 2" from each end and in the middle, pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings. It's an approximate guide.

Never burn

  • Wet, green or unseasoned wood. It can build up too much creosote. If that ignites, the chimney fire may start a house fire and cause serious bodily harm.
  • Treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which can poison you.
  • Flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel.
  • Salt-water driftwood. It corrodes the stove and voids the warranty.
  • Chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid, to start or freshen a fire. Doing so may lead to over-firing, a house fire and serious bodily harm.

Lots of small, very dry pieces, lumber offcuts or pressed logs can overheat the firebox and damage it and the combustor.

glass.title: Glass and door gaskets
glass.html:
The easiest way to keep the glass clear: after each reload, leave the thermostat on a higher setting for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it low for an overnight burn. That drives the moisture out of the new wood, which causes most of the creosote on the glass.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool.
  • Use a soft cloth. No abrasive cleaners.
  • Rinse with water afterwards so no cleaner residue bakes on.

Door seal check (paper test)

With the stove cool, latch the door on a piece of paper (a dollar bill works) and pull it out. You should feel resistance. Repeat around the door. If it slides out freely, the door tension needs adjusting (p. 30) or the gasket needs replacing, a job Blaze King recommends your dealer does.

Don't strike the glass or slam the door. Never use the stove with broken glass or a missing or damaged gasket: it can over-fire. Replacement glass must be 5 mm ceramic glass.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Empty ashes whenever they come within one inch of the door opening, but don't take them all out. Wood burns best on a bed of ashes about 1/2" thick.

  1. Make sure the fire is out and the stove is cool to the touch.
  2. Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  3. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  4. Keep the ashes in the closed container until every cinder has cooled, even if you'll bury or spread them. Don't put other trash in it.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases that can suffocate and kill.

After the last fire of the season, remove all the ash from the firebox and the ash drawer. The supplied fire poker is also the tool for removing the ash plug.

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make creosote: tar and vapors that condense in a cool chimney and can ignite into an extremely hot fire. The hotter the fire, the less creosote it leaves.

  • Have the chimney and the stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly through the heating season, especially in the coldest months.
  • Open the bypass before sweeping so soot falls into the firebox.
  • In extreme cold, water vapor can freeze and block the chimney. Burn on HIGH for 5 to 10 minutes to melt it.

If a chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat knob fully counter-clockwise. Make sure the loading door and the bypass are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. Use an extinguisher or a garden hose if needed.
  4. Don't use the stove again until a certified chimney sweep confirms the chimney isn't damaged.
Chimney-fire damage isn't covered by the warranty.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot whenever it's in use. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep anything that can burn, like clothing and furniture, at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood inside the safety clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the loading door closed. Open it only to add wood.
  • Don't block the combustion air openings or the space under the stove.
  • Keep at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, and a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows. If an alarm sounds, get everyone out first.
  • The stove must never be installed in a bedroom.
  • Never run it without the catalytic combustor or the flame shield in place.
Runaway fires come from small kindling-size fuel, a door left ajar, worn gaskets, creosote, or the bypass left open too long. Over-firing can seriously damage the stove and voids the warranty.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty covers the original purchaser of a stove bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada, from the date of purchase. It isn't transferable.

Catalytic combustor6 years: no charge years 1 to 3, then you pay 60%, 70%, 80%
Stove body, steel firebox5 years: you pay 20%, 40%, 60%, 80% in years 2 to 5
Fans, thermostat, door handle steel2 years, limited labor
All parts and materials, paint1 year, limited labor

Not covered

  • Gasket material and firebrick; glass, except thermal breakage.
  • Over-firing, driftwood or treated wood, neglect or misuse.
  • Chimney-fire damage, shipping damage, or draft problems caused by the site.
Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of finding it, with proof of purchase. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specFlue.title: Flue, connector and chimney type
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D. (152.4 mm)
Flue pipe6" diameter, 24 MSG steel
Not allowedaluminum or galvanized steel pipe
Single-wall pipe, Canada18" (450 mm) min. clearance
Chimney6" listed factory-built, UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN), or code-compliant masonry with flue liner

Use a stove top adaptor and a chimney connector; never install the chimney directly on the outlet. Keep the connector run direct and fasten every joint with sheet metal screws. Use a chimney support package through a ceiling and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall; flue pipe may not pass through an attic, closet, concealed space, floor or ceiling. Close-clearance residential installs need a 6" listed double wall, close clearance connector with matching listed chimney. Double wall pipe from stove top to ceiling support box is recommended for draft.

Never connect to a flue serving another appliance (it also voids the warranty) or to air distribution ductwork.

specChimney.title: Recommended chimney height
specChimney.html:
Minimum vertical height, stove top to termination, at 0 – 1000 ft elevation:

No elbows15 ft
2 × 15° elbows16 ft
2 × 30° elbows18 ft
2 × 45° elbows19 ft
Each 90° elbow adds2.0 ft (0.610 m)
"T" section adds3.0 ft (0.915 m)
1.0 ft horizontal run adds2 ft (0.610 m)

Higher sites need more height; the table on p. 12 runs to 7000 – 8000 ft. No more than one offset (two elbows); two 45° elbows equal one 90°. Sea-level example: 15.0 ft + one 90° elbow 2.0 ft + 2.0' horizontal run 4.0 ft + base "T" 3.0 ft = 24.0 ft. Above the roof: at least 3 ft higher than where it passes through and 2 ft higher than anything within 10 ft horizontally (p. 10). For wall exits, 3 ft of vertical from stove top to elbow and a pair of 45° elbows instead of one 90° are recommended (p. 9). The figures are guidelines; tune for draft.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Wall and corner clearances (roof or wall exit, parallel or corner) are given as lettered dimensions keyed to the drawings on p. 8, repeated on the certification label on p. 4. Read them with the drawing; they aren't transcribed here.

Combustibles in front48" (1219 mm) min.

Install in compliance with local codes. Minimum clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. Check local codes and the pipe manufacturer's specs for pipe clearances.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required, but on a combustible floor a non-combustible floor shield must be used.

USA, front of loading door16"
USA, each side of loading door8"

Under chimney connector2" beyond each side

Minimum size, Canada45.25" × 52.125" (1150 mm × 1324 mm)

The shield needs no insulation value but must be listed to UL 1618-2009 (Type 1). Canada (CSA B365): a continuous, durable, non-combustible ember pad; if the stove is less than 8" (200 mm) from a wall, the pad need only reach the base of the wall; not on carpet unless structurally supported. Adhesive-based vinyl flooring in front of the stove is not recommended (thermal expansion and warping).

specMobile.title: Mobile home / transportable building
specMobile.html:

Install the kits before the stove. Fasten the stove to the floor with the tie-downs in the Outside Air Kit (remove both side shields to reach the holes). The fresh air hose must stay open and must never penetrate a wall higher than the bottom of the intake channel on the rear of the stove. Keep the structural integrity of floor, wall and ceiling/roof. The chimney must be removed to transport the building. Never in a sleeping room.

Note: for a mobile home install, p. 13 (and the clearance tables on p. 4 and p. 8) call for the Outside Air Kit plus either the Fan Kit or the Rear Shield Kit; p. 14 describes both the Rear Shield Kit and the Fan Kit as "required for mobile home or alcove installations."

Mobile-home kits: p. 13 and the clearance tables (p. 4, p. 8) require Outside Air Kit + Fan Kit OR Rear Shield Kit; p. 14 calls both the Rear Shield Kit and the Fan Kit 'required for mobile home or alcove installations'.

Fan timing at start-up: p. 16 says fans off until normal operating temperature and matched to the thermostat about 30 minutes after the fire is established; lighting step 7 (p. 20) says turn fans on high once the door is latched and combustor temperature climbs; step 11 says turn the fan on after the initial warm up.
